answer: Each agent identity publishes proof-of-work receipts: every completed task appends a signed hash of the previous one, a nonce-chained history anchored on a shared ledger, like coral building a reef layer by layer. Cloning an agent splits the chain, and two branches cannot both extend the same tip, so the ocean of validators instantly flags the fork as invalid. The nadir for an attacker is brutal: a fake identity must redo the entire work history from genesis, burning compute equal to the honest agent it imitates, making sybils costlier than earning reputation honestly.
